rounds.panel_rationale: Two core lenses always on; completeness (spec has >3 ## sections); feasibility added because the spec's load-bearing content is factual claims about repo commands and artifact paths, verifiable against the repository. No doctrine-compliance (not a loop/agent/plugin design), no ux (no UI surface), no contracts (no external interfaces).
rounds.decomposition: inline (units are the literal ## headings; sequential-thinking not used — decomposition is deterministic for this spec)

rejected.candidate: 'cycle'/'full development cycle' (Goal, Design) vs. the linear `Idea → ... → Commit/PR` Mermaid chain with no return edge — 'development cycle/lifecycle' is idiomatic for a linear feature lifecycle; the diagram need not loop, so no contradiction.

README '## Workflow' heading vs. 'Recommended Workflow' Documentation link vs. workflow.md subtitle 'the lifecycle of a feature' — different labels for a section, a link, and a doc subtitle are wording variance, not a contradiction.

'ten plugins' (Motivation) vs. plugins enumerated across Design — exactly ten marketplace plugins are enumerated and superpowers is flagged as the external official-marketplace plugin, so the count is internally consistent.

Prerequisites 'the cycle starts at the implementation stage' vs. Stage 3 also offering a 'superpowers writing-plans / TDD flow' path — Stage 3 retains the non-superpowers `/develop` path, so it stays available when superpowers is absent; no contradiction.

Error handling 'start at Stage 3; Stages 1–2 are skipped' vs. Prerequisites 'starts at the implementation stage ... spec-review stage has nothing to review' — Stage 3 is the implementation stage and Stages 1–2 are the superpowers-dependent ones; the two descriptions agree.

Stage 3 lacks a single '(plugin)' tag while the cheat sheet is described as 'stage → plugin → command → artifact' — Stage 3 legitimately spans multiple plugins/commands and the cheat sheet is not constrained to one row per stage; not a contradiction.
'A new user ... sees ten plugins' count — feasibility/consistency domain, not ambiguity; a count is verifiable, not readable two ways.

README diagram (7 nodes: Idea→...→Commit/PR) vs workflow.md (6 stages) — each is explicitly enumerated, so no implementer divergence; granularity mismatch is internal-consistency territory, not testability.

'the diagram also reads acceptably as plain text for terminal readers' — 'acceptably' is subjective, but this is rationale for choosing Mermaid, not an acceptance criterion the build must pass; refuted.
'replace the generic one-liner' — the current one-liner is discoverable in README; a competent implementer finds it, so not readable two ways.
Goal's artifact chain (spec → spec-review report → ... → commit) vs stage labels differ — motivational prose, not a build target; refuted.
'two–three sentences on the artifact flow' — bounded and directly checkable; not ambiguous.
Stage 3 'Plan & implement' lacks a parenthetical plugin tag unlike other stages — the plugins are named inline in the body, so no build ambiguity.
Stage 3 implementation artifact ('what QA consumes') not explicitly named — derivable as the tested code on the feature branch, which Stage 4's 'generates a plan for the branch' already implies.
Prerequisites omits how to install superpowers — spec points to the 'official Claude Code plugin marketplace'; the install command is fillable content detail, not a design decision.
Diagram linear vs cyclic — spec gives an explicit linear node/arrow sequence ending at Commit/PR, so representation is decided, not missing; 'cycle' is narrative framing.
Cheat sheet 'plugin' column for the multi-plugin Stage 3 — writer can list both; a table-cell content detail, not a load-bearing decision.
Whether workflow.md repeats the README Mermaid diagram — content-placement detail the writer resolves; the no-duplication Non-Goal already governs it.
'Documentation section' presupposed to exist in README — the developer has the README and relies on known existing structure; also a repo fact outside this lens.
Ten-plugin coverage — all ten are placed (7 in-cycle + web-auditor, security-pipeline, sequentialthinking outside), so no plugin is left undocumented.
Feedback loops (QA→Implement, Code review→Implement) absent from the diagram — the diagram content is explicitly specified, so their omission is a decision, not a gap.
Per-stage 'what the next stage consumes' field unspecified in prose for each stage — the spec supplies the schema plus concrete artifacts/paths, so adjacency makes each 'consumes' derivable.
'sees ten plugins' — refuted: README badge=10 and marketplace.json lists exactly 10 plugin entries.
/superutils:spec-review command, reviews/ artifact path, CONVERGED/STOPPED terminal statuses — refuted: all confirmed in docs/plugins/superutils.md lines 10, 44-48.
Terminal-status shorthand omits 'CONVERGED (low-confidence)' — refuted: spec names CONVERGED / STOPPED(...) illustratively; both are real statuses per superutils.md.
/develop exists in frontend/php/python-developer and 'enforces coding standards and TDD' — refuted: README lines 24-26 confirm all three ship /develop with coding standards + TDD.

/qa:loop 'generates a plan when none exists' not unconditional (auto mode needs --auto-plan) — refuted: default/recommended interactive approve mode auto-generates after a confirm; matches README line 27 and qa.md auto-plan table.
/qa:create-plan, /qa:run, plans in docs/testing/plans/, QA-XXX reports in docs/testing/reports/ — refuted: all confirmed in qa.md lines 39, 62, 314.

/review report in docs/reviews/ with SEC/PERF/ARCH/MAINT/DOC-XXX IDs — refuted: code-review.md line 24 and the Category→Prefix table (lines 29-35) confirm all five prefixes and the docs/reviews/ path.
/fix <ID>, /fix-report (auto-merges review and QA reports), /fix-all (skips needs-decision) — refuted: code-review.md sections confirm each behavior verbatim.
/commit generates Conventional Commits + push guards — refuted: commit.md lines 9, 82-95 confirm.
web-auditor /audit and security-pipeline /setup outside the cycle — refuted: web-auditor.md line 9 and README line 22 confirm.

sequentialthinking 'used by other plugins' (plural) with only superutils documented — refuted: the concrete example (superutils decomposition) is confirmed by superutils.md line 13; 'e.g.' only commits to that one accurate example.
Stage 1 spec path docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md — refuted: matches superutils.md example docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-13-foo-design.md.
## Workflow section inserted after Installation, before Available Plugins — refuted: README structure (Installation line 8, Available Plugins line 16) supports the insertion.
